National Petroleum Co Ltd Announces Major Investment to Expand Oil Production Capacity in Egypt

National Petroleum Co Ltd has unveiled plans to invest $250 million in the expansion of its oil production facilities in Egypt’s Western Desert, aiming to boost output and support the country’s growing energy sector. The project, set to commence in the third quarter of 2024, will focus on upgrading existing infrastructure and drilling additional wells across the company’s operating fields.

“The investment reflects our long-term commitment to Egypt and our confidence in the resource potential of the Western Desert,” said Mahmoud El-Sharif, Managing Director of National Petroleum Co Ltd, during a press briefing in Cairo on Wednesday. “We anticipate an increase in production capacity by approximately 15% over the next two years, which will contribute significantly to both local supply and export volumes.”

Industry observers have welcomed the move, noting the positive impact on Egypt’s oil output and local employment. “This expansion aligns with Egypt’s broader strategy to strengthen its position as a regional energy hub,” commented Rania Fathy, an energy analyst at the Cairo-based consultancy MedEnergy Insights. “It’s also likely to create hundreds of jobs during the construction and operational phases.”

According to the Egyptian General Petroleum Authority, oil production in the Western Desert currently represents more than 50% of the nation’s crude output. National Petroleum Co Ltd’s expansion is expected to leverage advanced extraction technologies while adhering to strict environmental and safety standards.

Local suppliers are also poised to benefit. Ahmed Mostafa, chairman of Delta Engineering Services, a contractor working with National Petroleum Co Ltd, stated, “Our collaboration will see increased demand for equipment and services, supporting the local supply chain.”

The company emphasized its ongoing commitment to environmental stewardship, highlighting plans to implement water recycling and emissions reduction measures as part of the expansion. The project is expected to reach full operational capacity by late 2026.
